hypotheses.subject: 9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e
hypotheses.summary: The deploy of revision 9f4c1e7b2a3d5c8e1f0b6a4d2c9e7b5a3f1d8c6e at 15:06 introduced a latency regression: the very next minute p95 began climbing (220ms -> 900ms -> 1800ms -> 5000ms) and errors rose to 12% as requests started timing out. It is the only recorded change to io-shop in the month before the incident.

supporting_evidence.claim: Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-08-12T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-12T15:06:00Z - contains only the 15:06 deploy; no other change, and no feature-flag toggle, in the preceding month.
WARN io-shop: p95 latency at 1800ms, up from a 220ms baseline

hypotheses.summary: No cause is positively identified by the retrieved evidence: the logs carry only generic latency/timeout lines with no error detail, dependency name, or flag name, and the only change in view is a deploy whose contents are not described. The 15:06 deploy is temporally adjacent but the correlation is all there is; a slow dependency or resource exhaustion unrelated to the deploy would produce the same latency-then-timeout shape.

supporting_evidence.claim: Log window 2026-09-12T15:04:00Z to 2026-09-12T15:09:49Z contains only "request succeeded", "p95 latency climbing", "p95 latency at 1800ms, up from a 220ms baseline", and "request timeout after 5000ms" - no stack trace, downstream name, flag name, or config value.
Log lines from 2026-09-12T15:09:49Z to 2026-09-12T15:30:00Z: (no log lines in this window) - no post-alert evidence such as a rollback and recovery to confirm the deploy.
